summary: Prompt provided to Claude Opus to create a 1990s-style demoscene demo synchronized to an S3M music track using C/C++ and OpenGL.

post.originalText:
Opus 5.5 just one-shot this 90s-style demoscene demo for me. It's pretty good.
It's a genuine one-shot (in colloquial X post sense - single prompt) and my first attempt asking it to do such a thing. I just supplied Purple Motion's music from Second Reality. C/C++ and OpenGL. https://t.co/yH2GEnfCNw

sourceMaterials.text: @Tempivagus Some people are getting upset with a showcase of inevitable technology achieving something roughly similar to competitive demonstrations from 33 years ago (which I do know how to write - for those who care). I really don't want to be like them. I really, really don't.
sourceMaterials.author: gandamu_ml

sourceMaterials.text: @Dean_Woodyatt It used <3% of the week's quota, but it is Claude Max.
sourceMaterials.author: gandamu_ml

sourceMaterials.text: @BugoTheCat @_itmo_ On the other hand I understand the criticism of the specific demos, because I made three of them that I prefer while screwing around with AI demos for the first time today.
sourceMaterials.author: gandamu_ml

sourceMaterials.text:
@BugoTheCat @_itmo_ I understand the disappointment in it because it's a way to compete and show off (while making something cool in the process).. and all those things disrupt the competitive standard and undercut the process.
Complaining about prods in the AI category is a bit rude though imo 😄
sourceMaterials.author: gandamu_ml

sourceMaterials.text:
@QINGCHARLES I think it's a simple task for it now. My prompt said it should blit pixels for some of it but could use OpenGL for some stuff.
If it made a software rasterizer for everything it could end being even cooler though.
sourceMaterials.author: gandamu_ml

sourceMaterials.text: @_itmo_ @BugoTheCat really? That seems needed. Must be tough to determine what isn't vibecoded now though. Honor system I guess.
sourceMaterials.author: gandamu_ml

sourceMaterials.text:
@LinuxJedi I was surprised it decided to do that, so the prompt didn't include anything for a CRT effect. With some good prompting for it, it might do a decent job.

In any case, it's notable that there are things that it won't automatically do very well without instruction.
sourceMaterials.author: gandamu_ml

sourceMaterials.text: @antedgemon Cool. I used to encounter the Mars demo a lot, but I hadn't seen Sean Barrett's.
sourceMaterials.author: gandamu_ml

sourceMaterials.text: @gamedevsam I was somewhat impressed even before it zoomed into a layer. Nice.
sourceMaterials.author: gandamu_ml

sourceMaterials.text:
@realPaulMJ @NerdWorldOrder @TrillStancil All in all, this is being pretty well-received tbh.. or at least, received primarily as just news that it can do this.

I'd just seen people sharing p5.js animations made by Claude and I was curious how well it would do something more like a demoscene demo.
sourceMaterials.author: gandamu_ml

sourceMaterials.text:
@realPaulMJ @NerdWorldOrder @TrillStancil This demo (executable + S3M) is about the same size as Second Reality. It's 1.5MB on macos vs Second Reality's ~1.44MB (iirc) on MSDOS. If I compiled it with different flags or on Windows, this new one would be the smaller one.
Second Reality had more content. I could make this much smaller as an exercise, but then people would be even less happy about it.
sourceMaterials.author: gandamu_ml

sourceMaterials.text: @BugoTheCat I really think the biggest thing stopping it from upending life is the inertia of organizations. This is our best moderator of progress. Maybe we really are at least somewhat benefiting from it a bit for once. Not great in terms of global competition, but keeps life simpler.
sourceMaterials.author: gandamu_ml

sourceMaterials.text:
@BugoTheCat The program generated by Opus 5.5 here cost me a little under $1.40 (as a weighted proportion of my monthly subscription). This is because it was under 3% of my weekly usage.
So at its strengths (and it has many now), the cost is insignificant compared to human labor+time cost.
sourceMaterials.author: gandamu_ml
gandamu_ml

sourceMaterials.text: @NoctreSharp * similar to most people not knowing what "demo" means without saying "demoscene demo", most people also wouldn't know what was meant by "intro" without the qualifier. Now I've explained why I used the word.
sourceMaterials.author: gandamu_ml

sourceMaterials.text:
@NoctreSharp That's a different task. Lots of demos (as opposed to *intros) are well over 1MB now so the 1.5MB size of this isn't an issue.
You're just being rude, like most people. This is acceptable to you and them.
sourceMaterials.author: gandamu_ml

sourceMaterials.text:
@0zz0zz0zz0zz0 Purple Motion did the most (and most time), Opus 5.5 second (3hrs 10min), me last (placed 2ND_PM.S3M in a folder and spent 2 minutes typing a prompt).
There isn't an intellectual claim here but today's AI abilities are news. I'd say this is more important than most of the news.
sourceMaterials.author: gandamu_ml
gandamu_ml

sourceMaterials.text: @gr_oc @BugoTheCat As for previously having been someone writing realtime gfx code in asm.. and now using AI to write things.. It's the powerful technology of our time. It's even a new artform of our time! There is nothing inconsistent here. With the pace of change today, locking in time is unwise.
sourceMaterials.author: gandamu_ml

sourceMaterials.text: @gr_oc @BugoTheCat i.e. there is no surprise here. I want to be a part of things getting better, or at least towards people reaching inevitable conclusions sooner.
sourceMaterials.author: gandamu_ml
